outcome.shown: Earth's seasons are caused by the 23.5-degree tilt of its rotational axis combined with its orbital motion around the Sun. As the planet travels along its yearly path, this axial tilt means that different hemispheres receive varying amounts of direct sunlight at different times of the year. When a hemisphere is tilted toward the Sun, it experiences summer due to longer days and more concentrated solar rays, while the opposite hemisphere is tilted away, resulting in shorter days, less direct sunlight, and winter.
